AI.conclusion: Polymer quantization on compact configuration spaces yields discrete graph-based Hilbert spaces distinct from the Schrödinger representation, but the continuum limit recovers standard quantum mechanical results, validating the approach as an alternative quantization scheme.

title: Barbell Codes: qLDPC Codes for Superconducting Quantum Hardware

summary: The major challenge on the way to fault-tolerant quantum computing comes from the insufficient quality of hardware components and the difficulty of scaling their number without further compromising fidelity. Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (qLDPC) codes offer a promising solution by encoding logical qubits with low overhead and at a comparatively high code distance. However, it remains an open question how to scalably implement efficient qLDPC codes on fixed-connectivity quantum chips without increasing hardware complexity to enable the non-local interactions in their underlying QEC cycles. We resolve this challenge for the first time by introducing a family of qLDPC "barbell" codes accompanied by a realistic chip layout that natively supports all required two-qubit interactions. Crucially, the hardware complexity required to implement barbell codes remains constant as code distance increases. We provide a detailed investigation into the feasibility of all required hardware components and simulate a specific family of barbell codes against circuit-level noise. We find that, with a modest overhead of $<30$ data qubits per logical qubit, barbell codes can preserve information at a physical noise strength of $10^{-4}$ for several trillion QEC cycles. Simulations of logical multi-Pauli measurements, performed with circuits tailored to the chip, yield similar logical performance per QEC round, indicating that entangling gates between logical qubits in barbell codes can be realized fault-tolerantly.

AI.motivation: The major challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computing is insufficient hardware quality and difficulty scaling components without fidelity loss. While qLDPC codes promise low-overhead error correction, implementing them scalably on fixed-connectivity chips without increasing hardware complexity for non-local interactions remains an open problem.
AI.method: The authors introduce a family of qLDPC "barbell" codes with a realistic chip layout that natively supports all required two-qubit interactions while keeping hardware complexity constant as code distance increases. They perform detailed feasibility analysis of required hardware components and simulate barbell codes against circuit-level noise, including logical multi-Pauli measurements with tailored circuits.
AI.result: With fewer than 30 data qubits per logical qubit, barbell codes preserve information at physical noise strength 10^-4 for trillions of QEC cycles. Logical multi-Pauli measurements yield similar logical performance per QEC round, indicating fault-tolerant entangling gates between logical qubits.
AI.conclusion: Barbell codes resolve the challenge of implementing efficient qLDPC codes on fixed-connectivity quantum chips with constant hardware complexity, paving the way for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing with low overhead.

title: Forbidden transitions in superconducting artificial atoms
summary: Artificial atoms built from Josephson junctions have become a powerful tool to explore the limits of quantum optics due to their strong coupling to electromagnetic fields and their sensitivity to changes at the single-photon level. This sensitivity to quantum fluctuations complements their metrological and computational use, which are based on the precise oscillating frequency of the underlying supercurrents. We present here a theory for Josephson junctions immersed in electromagnetic fields where focus is shifted from temporal correlations and towards spatial ones. Unlike the commonly used circuit and black-box descriptions, our work is based on a microscopic model that enables systematically accounting for the effect of the spatial and vectorial profile of an electromagnetic field over a junction. As an example of the interactions that emerge in such a setup, we investigate the possibility of driving a junction via a quadrupole transition, using typical experimental parameters in existing devices. With the transition being dependent on the gradient of the electric field -- rather than its intensity -- the junction can be excited in a region where the electric field vanishes.

AI.tldr: A microscopic theory for Josephson junctions in electromagnetic fields is presented, shifting focus from temporal to spatial correlations, and demonstrating quadrupole-driven transitions in regions where electric field vanishes.
AI.motivation: To develop a microscopic model for Josephson junctions in electromagnetic fields that accounts for spatial and vectorial field profiles, moving beyond conventional circuit and black-box descriptions.
AI.method: A microscopic theoretical model that systematically incorporates the spatial and vectorial profile of electromagnetic fields over a Josephson junction, shifting focus from temporal to spatial correlations.
AI.result: Demonstrates the possibility of driving a Josephson junction via a quadrupole transition using typical experimental parameters, where the transition depends on the electric field gradient rather than intensity.
AI.conclusion: The spatial approach enables new interaction regimes, such as exciting a junction where the electric field vanishes via quadrupole transitions, expanding the quantum optics toolbox for superconducting circuits.

title: Efficient Quantum Circuit Construction of Controlled Time-Evolution for Arbitrary Pauli-Sum Hamiltonians
summary: Controlled time-evolution circuits select forward or backward Hamiltonian time evolution according to the state of an ancilla qubit. They are fundamental building blocks in quantum eigenvalue transformation of unitaries, Hamiltonian filtering, and related quantum algorithms. A direct realization adds ancilla control to the elementary gates of the time-evolution circuit and therefore increases the two-qubit gate count, compiled T depth and CX depth. We develop an efficient recursive algorithm that, for an arbitrary Pauli-sum Hamiltonian, partitions the input Pauli terms into groups and assigns to each group a sign-flip Pauli string that anti-commutes with the in-group terms, thereby removing ancilla control from the grouped time-evolution blocks. Numerical benchmarks on random Hamiltonians and structured spin Hamiltonians show reductions in compiled T depth and compiled CX depth. For a Kagome Hamiltonian with 24 spins under full connectivity, the proposed construction reduces the compiled T depth by 85.2% and the compiled CX depth by 68.9%, compared with a conventional implementation that decomposes the Hamiltonian into individual Pauli terms and implements the controlled time evolution of each term by directly adding the ancilla qubit to the corresponding Pauli-rotation circuit.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an efficient recursive algorithm that partitions Pauli-sum Hamiltonian terms into groups, assigns sign-flip Pauli strings to each group to remove ancilla control from controlled time-evolution circuits, achieving significant reductions in compiled T depth (up to 85.2%) and CX depth (up to 68.9%) for structured spin Hamiltonians like Kagome with 24 spins.
AI.motivation: Controlled time-evolution circuits are fundamental for quantum eigenvalue transformation and Hamiltonian filtering, but direct realization increases two-qubit gate count, T depth, and CX depth. The goal is to reduce these overheads by eliminating ancilla control from grouped time-evolution blocks.
AI.method: A recursive algorithm that partitions input Pauli terms into groups and assigns to each group a sign-flip Pauli string that anti-commutes with all in-group terms, enabling removal of ancilla control from grouped time-evolution blocks.
AI.result: Numerical benchmarks on random Hamiltonians and structured spin Hamiltonians show reductions in compiled T depth and CX depth. For a Kagome Hamiltonian with 24 spins under full connectivity, compiled T depth reduced by 85.2% and compiled CX depth by 68.9% compared to the conventional per-term ancilla-controlled Pauli rotation approach.
AI.conclusion: The proposed group-based ancilla control removal significantly reduces quantum resource requirements for controlled time-evolution circuits, making them more practical for quantum algorithms relying on eigenvalue transformation and Hamiltonian filtering.

title: Quantum-limited estimation of atmospheric turbulence via spatial mode decomposition
summary: We establish the ultimate precision limit for estimating the optical spatial coherence radius (Fried parameter) within a quantum metrological framework. In the weak field regime, we show that spatial-mode decomposition -- originally introduced for superresolution imaging -- enables substantially more precise estimation than conventional direct imaging when the receiver aperture is smaller than the coherence radius.

AI.tldr: Establishes ultimate precision limit for estimating the Fried parameter via quantum metrology, showing spatial-mode decomposition outperforms direct imaging for small apertures in the weak field regime.
AI.motivation: To determine the fundamental quantum-limited precision for estimating optical spatial coherence (Fried parameter) and to identify whether advanced measurement strategies (spatial-mode decomposition) can surpass conventional direct imaging in the weak-field regime.
AI.method: Quantum metrological framework applied to the estimation of the Fried parameter; comparison of spatial-mode decomposition (from superresolution imaging) versus conventional direct imaging, analyzed specifically in the weak-field regime and for receiver apertures smaller than the coherence radius.
AI.result: Spatial-mode decomposition yields substantially more precise estimation than direct imaging when the receiver aperture is smaller than the coherence radius.
AI.conclusion: Spatial-mode decomposition offers a significant precision advantage over direct imaging for estimating the Fried parameter under sub-aperture coherence conditions, establishing a new quantum-limited benchmark for coherence sensing.

title: Deployed trusted-node quantum key distribution over 300 km with a multi-core fiber access link
summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is increasingly considered for deployment in realistic communication networks, where long distances, heterogeneous fiber infrastructure, and coexistence with classical traffic present substantial challenges. Here, we demonstrate trusted-node QKD between Linköping University and the Stockholm hub of the Swedish national quantum communication infrastructure over 270 km of deployed single-mode fiber, extended by a 33 km multi-core fiber (MCF) segment emulating a metropolitan access link, for a total distance of 303 km. The two sub-links use commercial QKD systems whose receivers are interfaced with external superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, enabling operation at losses beyond those supported by standard internal gated-mode detectors. We operate the link while actively switching the QKD channel between two MCF cores, with co-propagating Ethernet traffic and injected broadband optical noise in the other cores. The results demonstrate the integration of commercial QKD into demanding, dynamically reconfigurable fiber infrastructure relevant to future hybrid quantum-classical networks. Finally, using the generated secret keys, we illustrate how limited and time-varying QKD throughput affects one-time-pad-protected image transmission: image fidelity depends strongly on the available QKD-generated key budget and the choice of compression algorithm, highlighting application-level challenges for QKD-based encryption in realistic scenarios.

AI.tldr: The authors demonstrate trusted-node QKD over 303 km of deployed fiber (270 km single-mode + 33 km multi-core fiber) in Sweden, using commercial QKD systems with external superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, active core switching, and co-existing classical traffic, and analyze how limited QKD key rates affect one-time-pad image transmission fidelity.
AI.motivation: To validate the feasibility of deploying QKD in realistic, long-distance, heterogeneous fiber networks with coexisting classical data traffic, and to understand application-level challenges (e.g., image encryption) under practical, time-varying key generation constraints.
AI.method: Commercial QKD systems with external superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) replace standard gated-mode detectors to handle higher channel loss. A 270 km single-mode fiber link plus a 33 km multi-core fiber (MCF) segment emulates a metropolitan access link. Active optical switching between two MCF cores is performed while Ethernet traffic and broadband noise are injected in other cores.
AI.result: Successful trusted-node QKD over a total distance of 303 km of deployed fiber, with active core switching and coexistence with classical Ethernet traffic and injected optical noise. The external SNSPDs enable operation at losses beyond the capability of internal gated-mode detectors.
AI.conclusion: Commercial QKD can be integrated into demanding, dynamically reconfigurable fiber infrastructures. However, limited and time-varying QKD throughput strongly affects one-time-pad encrypted image transmission fidelity, depending on the key budget and compression algorithm chosen, highlighting important application-layer challenges for real-world QKD-based encryption.

title: Semidefinite-programming hierarchies for classically simulable state families
summary: Identifying whether a state family admits an irreducible quantum advantage is a fundamental task in quantum resource theory and quantum information processing. Here we study classically simulable state families, namely those residing within the convex hull of pairwise commuting families and therefore admitting a classical explanation. We develop a complete semidefinite-programming (SDP) hierarchy characterizing the set of classically simulable state families in arbitrary finite dimension. The key step is to reformulate classical simulability as a feasibility problem over deterministic response functions and auxiliary positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) simulable by rank-one projective measurements. We establish a complete SDP hierarchy for rank-one projectively simulable POVMs and transfer the resulting characterization to state families, yielding both primal feasibility tests and dual affine witnesses certifying failure of classical simulability. Applying the hierarchy to state families mixed with depolarizing noise gives computable upper bounds on the critical classical visibility, which are matched by explicit classical simulations in several symmetric examples. These results provide a systematic convex-optimization framework for certifying classical simulability of quantum state families.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a complete semidefinite-programming (SDP) hierarchy to characterize classically simulable quantum state families—those within the convex hull of pairwise commuting families—by reformulating classical simulability as a feasibility problem over deterministic response functions and rank-one projectively simulable POVMs, yielding both primal tests and dual witnesses for non-classicality.
AI.motivation: To systematically identify whether a quantum state family admits an irreducible quantum advantage, which is fundamental to quantum resource theory and quantum information processing.
AI.method: The authors reformulate classical simulability as a feasibility problem over deterministic response functions and auxiliary POVMs simulable by rank-one projective measurements. They establish a complete SDP hierarchy for rank-one projectively simulable POVMs and transfer this characterization to state families, producing primal feasibility tests and dual affine witnesses.
AI.result: For state families mixed with depolarizing noise, the hierarchy provides computable upper bounds on critical classical visibility, which are matched by explicit classical simulations in several symmetric examples.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a systematic convex-optimization framework for certifying classical simulability of quantum state families, with demonstrated tightness in symmetric cases.

title: Multiple Quantum Hypothesis Testing: One-Shot Pairwise Bounds and Sharp Asymptotics

summary:
We consider Bayesian discrimination among multiple quantum states and establish a dimension-free one-shot upper bound on the minimum probability of error in terms of the sum of pairwise errors. This resolves a conjecture of Audenaert and Mosonyi [J. Math. Phys. 55 (2014)] and improves the multiple quantum Chernoff bound of Li [Ann. Statist. 44 (2016)] by removing its dimension-dependent prefactor. In the asymptotic many-copy regime, our bound proves the achievability of the multiple quantum Chernoff distance for arbitrary separable Hilbert spaces, thereby settling the previously open infinite-dimensional case, and further yields constant-factor sharp asymptotics for the optimal error probability.
  In binary quantum hypothesis testing, we prove that the minimum error probability is characterized, up to universal constants, by a trace harmonic-mean quantity. Consequently, the optimal binary quantum error probability is within a factor of two of the optimal classical error probability for the associated Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions, complementing the lower bound of Nussbaum and Szkoła [Ann. Statist. 37 (2009)].

AI.tldr: The paper resolves a conjecture by Audenaert and Mosonyi, proving a dimension-free one-shot upper bound for Bayesian multi-state discrimination via pairwise error sums. It improves the multiple quantum Chernoff bound by removing dimension-dependent prefactors, settles the infinite-dimensional case in the asymptotic regime, and yields constant-factor sharp asymptotics. In binary quantum hypothesis testing, it shows the minimum error probability is characterized (up to universal constants) by a trace harmonic-mean, and is within a factor of two of the optimal classical error probability for Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions.
AI.motivation: To establish tighter, dimension-free bounds for Bayesian quantum state discrimination in both one-shot and asymptotic settings, resolving open conjectures and settling previously open infinite-dimensional cases.
AI.method: Derives a dimension-free one-shot upper bound on the minimum error probability expressed as a sum of pairwise errors, improving upon prior dimension-dependent Chernoff bounds. For binary hypothesis testing, uses a trace harmonic-mean quantity to characterize the error probability up to universal constants.
AI.result: Proves achievability of the multiple quantum Chernoff distance for arbitrary separable Hilbert spaces (including infinite-dimensional), yields constant-factor sharp asymptotics, and shows binary quantum error probability is within a factor of 2 of the optimal classical error probability for Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions.
AI.conclusion: The work provides fundamental limits for quantum state discrimination with improved bounds that are dimension-independent, resolving key conjectures and completing the theory for infinite-dimensional settings.

title: Non-equilibrium thermodynamics of collapse models in the strongly non-Gaussian regime
summary: Standard objective collapse models offer a unified approach to the quantum measurement problem but predict an unphysical, indefinite increase in the energy of the system. The dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model resolves this heating issue by introducing a linear friction mechanism. However, this modification induces complex, non-Gaussian phase-space dynamics. We rigorously establish the thermodynamic consistency of this friction mechanism -- extended to the CSL model -- across both weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes. Using the Wigner phase-space formalism, we go significantly beyond the quadratic approximation and, to bypass the failure of perturbative methods under strong dissipation, introduce a novel exact pseudo-spectral simulation approach. Our analysis reveals that the system subjected to the dDP mechanism does not thermalize, but rather settles into a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) where the asymptotic non-Gaussianity scales as the third power of the dissipation parameter $β$. By evaluating the Wigner entropy production, we confirm the thermodynamic validity of the model and demonstrate that highly sensitive information-theoretic quantities require exact numerical methods to accurately capture the key non-Gaussian tails of the distribution.

AI.tldr: The paper rigorously establishes the thermodynamic consistency of the dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model (extended to CSL) in both weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes. Using the Wigner formalism and a novel exact pseudo-spectral simulation method, it shows the system settles into a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) with asymptotic non-Gaussianity scaling as β³, confirming thermodynamic validity via Wigner entropy production, and demonstrating that exact numerical methods are needed to capture key non-Gaussian tails.
AI.motivation: Standard objective collapse models, while offering a unified solution to the quantum measurement problem, suffer from an unphysical indefinite energy increase (heating). The dissipative Diósi-Penrose model introduces a friction mechanism to resolve this, but its thermodynamic consistency—particularly in non-Gaussian regimes—had not been rigorously established.
AI.method: The authors use the Wigner phase-space formalism to go beyond the quadratic approximation. To overcome the failure of perturbative methods under strong dissipation, they introduce a novel exact pseudo-spectral simulation approach. They analyze the dDP model extended to the CSL model across both weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes.
AI.result: The system subjected to the dDP mechanism does not thermalize but instead settles into a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS). The asymptotic non-Gaussianity scales as the third power of the dissipation parameter β. Wigner entropy production confirms thermodynamic validity. Highly sensitive information-theoretic quantities require exact numerical methods to accurately capture key non-Gaussian tails.
AI.conclusion: The dissipative Diósi-Penrose friction mechanism is thermodynamically consistent. Exact numerical methods are essential for accurately capturing non-Gaussian features in strongly dissipative regimes of objective collapse models.

title: Quantum Algorithms for Triangle Cut Sparsification
summary:
Triangles capture higher-order structures in graphs and are fundamental to applications such as clustering and network analysis.
  To enable efficient use of such structures at scale, we study the problem of \emph{triangle cut sparsification}, which aims to reduce the graph size while approximately preserving triangle counts across every cut.
  We investigate \emph{quantum algorithms} for this problem, using triangle listing as our main technical ingredient.
  In particular, we present a quantum algorithm for triangle listing that, for a graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and $t$ triangles, runs in time $T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} =$ $\widetilde{O}\bigl(\min(n^{5/4}t^{7/12} + n^{7/6}t^{7/9}, m + m^{3/4}t^{1/2},$ $n^{3/2}t^{1/2})\bigr)$, improving upon the best known classical bounds over a broad range of parameters. Our algorithm is based on a heavy-light vertex partition and an extension of triangle detection via quantum walks and Grover search.
  Leveraging this result, we design a quantum algorithm for constructing $\varepsilon$-triangle cut sparsifiers of size $\widetilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^2)$ in time $\widetilde{O}(T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} + \sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)$.
  Finally, we demonstrate applications to clustering algorithms based on triangle-related measures
  and prove a lower bound of $Ω(n/\varepsilon^2)$ on the size of any $\varepsilon$-triangle cut sparsifiers.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces quantum algorithms for triangle cut sparsification, presenting a faster quantum triangle listing algorithm (improving over classical bounds) and using it to construct ε-triangle cut sparsifiers of size Õ(n/ε²), with applications to clustering and a matching lower bound.
AI.motivation: Triangles capture higher-order graph structures that are essential for clustering and network analysis, but efficient use at scale requires reducing graph size while preserving triangle counts across cuts—hence the need for triangle cut sparsification.
AI.method: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for triangle listing based on a heavy-light vertex partition and quantum walks/Grover search, achieving runtime Õ(min(n^{5/4}t^{7/12}+n^{7/6}t^{7/9}, m+m^{3/4}t^{1/2}, n^{3/2}t^{1/2})). This is then used to construct ε-triangle cut sparsifiers in time Õ(T_q-list + √(mn)/ε).
AI.result: A quantum triangle listing algorithm improving upon classical bounds; a quantum algorithm for constructing ε-triangle cut sparsifiers of size Õ(n/ε²); and a lower bound of Ω(n/ε²) on the sparsifier size, showing optimality.
AI.conclusion: Quantum algorithms can provide significant speedups for triangle-based graph problems, enabling efficient sparsification that preserves higher-order structures, with applications to clustering algorithms based on triangle measures.

title: Quantum enhanced rare event discovery and sampling
summary: Financial crashes, cascading failures in infrastructure, and critical errors in AI systems are frequently triggered by events that occur with extremely small probability. Efficiently discovering and sampling events with probability below a threshold is therefore of critical interest. Yet this task is highly non-trivial using existing classical or quantum methods. Being rare, such events require an immense sampling overhead to collect sufficient data samples. Moreover, because the rare events are not known in advance, they cannot be flagged for amplification using standard techniques. Here, we introduce a quantum algorithm for rare-event discovery and sampling without first learning which events are rare. The algorithm achieves the optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold. We further demonstrate that this can achieve a quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems whose tail has nonvanishing total mass, and translates into a robust polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes, with the exponent determined by its entropy-rate structure.

AI.tldr: Introduces a quantum algorithm for discovering and sampling rare events (probability < threshold) without prior knowledge of which events are rare, achieving optimal quantum scaling and quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems and robust polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes.
AI.motivation: Financial crashes, infrastructure cascading failures, and AI system errors are triggered by extremely low-probability events. Efficiently discovering and sampling such rare events is critical but highly non-trivial with classical or quantum methods due to immense sampling overhead and the inability to pre-identify events for amplification.
AI.method: A quantum algorithm for rare-event discovery and sampling that does not require first learning which events are rare, achieving optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold.
AI.result: Achieves optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold; quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems with nonvanishing tail mass; robust polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes with exponent determined by entropy-rate structure.
AI.conclusion: The proposed quantum algorithm provides a provable advantage over classical methods for rare-event discovery and sampling across multiple domains, with speedups characterized by system-specific properties like tail behavior and entropy-rate structure.

title: Reliability of asymptotic work extraction
summary: Extracting work from quantum states is a fundamental task in quantum thermodynamics. Previous studies have primarily focused on determining the best achievable rate of work extraction, and remarkably, this characterization appeared to remain unchanged regardless of the choice of allowed processes: whether one considers the operationally motivated class of energy-conserving thermal operations, or the axiomatic class of Gibbs-preserving operations, the optimal extractable work is given by the Helmholtz free energy. Here, we challenge this perspective, showing that a more refined analysis of the asymptotic performance of work extraction reveals significant differences in the performance for the two different classes of free operations. Precisely, we focus on the trade-off between the extraction rate and its reliability, characterized by the optimal asymptotic speed at which the extraction error can be suppressed. We establish that the reliability of Gibbs-preserving operations and of thermal operations are respectively characterized by the Petz and the sandwiched Rényi relative entropies, demonstrating that the former in general strictly outperforms the latter, and providing new interpretations of several information-theoretic divergences. Our analysis reveals that operational constraints such as energy conservation impose stronger limitations on the achievable precision of quantum tasks than can be inferred from their asymptotic rates, thereby questioning the use of Gibbs-preserving operations as a mathematically convenient substitute for the physically realizable thermal processes.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the conventional view that thermal operations and Gibbs-preserving operations yield the same optimal work extraction rate (Helmholtz free energy), showing instead that when analyzing the reliability (error suppression speed) of work extraction, Gibbs-preserving operations strictly outperform thermal operations, with their respective performances characterized by Petz and sandwiched Rényi relative entropies.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the choice of allowed operations (energy-conserving thermal operations vs. axiomatic Gibbs-preserving operations) affects the asymptotic performance of quantum work extraction beyond the previously established optimal rate, specifically in terms of the trade-off between extraction rate and reliability (error suppression speed).
AI.method: The authors analyze the asymptotic performance of work extraction under two classes of free operations—thermal operations (energy-conserving) and Gibbs-preserving operations (axiomatic)—by characterizing the optimal asymptotic speed at which extraction error can be suppressed, using Petz and sandwiched Rényi relative entropies as the respective measures of reliability.
AI.result: The reliability of Gibbs-preserving operations and thermal operations are respectively characterized by the Petz Rényi relative entropy and the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy. Gibbs-preserving operations strictly outperform thermal operations in error suppression speed, demonstrating that operational energy-conservation constraints impose stronger limitations on achievable precision than asymptotic rates alone would suggest.
AI.conclusion: The use of Gibbs-preserving operations as a mathematically convenient substitute for physically realizable thermal processes is questionable when precision/reliability matters, as the operational constraint of energy conservation significantly limits achievable precision beyond what asymptotic rate analysis captures. The findings also provide new interpretations of several information-theoretic divergences.

title: Benchmarking Floquet Master Equations for Periodically Driven Open Quantum Systems
summary: The dynamics of open quantum systems is commonly described by quantum master equations derived under the assumption of weak system-bath coupling and a separation of timescales between system and bath. When the system is additionally subjected to a periodic driving, the validity of the resulting Floquet master equations is further restricted to regimes of weak or high-frequency driving. Here, we benchmark a set of commonly used Floquet master equations for a model of two locally driven spins coupled to a shared Ohmic reservoir at finite temperature. We systematically probe the accuracy of the equations as a function of the driving parameters, thus identifying limits of their applicability. Dynamical maps predicted by each master equation are compared against numerically exact non-Markovian simulations, tracking the full relaxation dynamics. We find that the accuracy of each master equation closely reflects the assumptions underlying its derivation. For the Floquet-Lindblad equation, errors can be strongly amplified near resonances where the secular approximation breaks down, while approaches that avoid the secular approximation perform better and exhibit a more systematic dependence of the error on driving frequency and amplitude.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks several Floquet master equations for open quantum systems under periodic driving, comparing them against numerically exact simulations for two driven spins coupled to an Ohmic reservoir. The accuracy of each equation reflects its underlying assumptions, with secular-approximation-based equations showing amplified errors near resonances, while non-secular approaches perform more robustly across driving parameters.
AI.motivation: To systematically benchmark the accuracy and identify the limits of applicability of commonly used Floquet master equations for driven open quantum systems, since their validity is often assumed but not rigorously tested across driving parameter regimes.
AI.method: A model of two locally driven spins coupled to a shared Ohmic reservoir at finite temperature is used. A set of commonly used Floquet master equations (including Floquet-Lindblad and approaches avoiding the secular approximation) are benchmarked by comparing their predicted dynamical maps against numerically exact non-Markovian simulations tracking the full relaxation dynamics. The accuracy is probed systematically as a function of driving parameters (frequency and amplitude).
AI.result: The accuracy of each master equation closely reflects the assumptions underlying its derivation. The Floquet-Lindblad equation exhibits strongly amplified errors near resonances where the secular approximation breaks down. Approaches that avoid the secular approximation perform better and show a more systematic dependence of error on driving frequency and amplitude.
AI.conclusion: Non-secular Floquet master equations are more reliable for driven open quantum systems, particularly near resonances, while secular-approximation-based equations (like Floquet-Lindblad) can become highly inaccurate in those regimes. Care must be taken when choosing a master equation, as the validity conditions are restrictive and depend sensitively on driving parameters.

title: A framework for low-overhead quantum fault tolerance via spacetime lifting
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computation is inherently a spacetime problem, requiring not merely good static quantum error-correcting codes but also low-overhead protocols for protecting and manipulating encoded quantum information over time. Fault complexes provide a homological framework for treating such protocols as single spacetime objects. In this work, we initiate the study of low-overhead fault complexes by introducing {spacetime lifting}, a method that constructs fault complexes from symmetry-reduced product structures beyond standard foliation. We show that spacetime lifting yields fault complexes and in particular {spacetime-lifted} memory experiments with almost-linear fault distance in the total spacetime cost, which substantially outperforms existing constructions. We further interpret fault complexes as measurement-based cluster-state protocols and identify general conditions under which they realize fault-tolerant logical teleportation, showing that spacetime-lifted constructions combine favorable scaling with operational schemes. Our study opens a path toward more efficient quantum fault tolerance through general complex constructions.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces "spacetime lifting," a method for constructing fault complexes (homological spacetime objects for fault-tolerant quantum computation) from symmetry-reduced product structures, achieving almost-linear fault distance in total spacetime cost—substantially outperforming existing constructions—and interprets these complexes as measurement-based cluster-state protocols for fault-tolerant logical teleportation.
AI.motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation is inherently a spacetime problem requiring low-overhead protocols for protecting and manipulating encoded quantum information over time. Existing constructions underperform, motivating a search for better homological frameworks (fault complexes) that treat protocols as single spacetime objects.
AI.method: The paper introduces "spacetime lifting," a method that constructs fault complexes from symmetry-reduced product structures beyond standard foliation. It further interprets fault complexes as measurement-based cluster-state protocols and identifies conditions for fault-tolerant logical teleportation.
AI.result: Spacetime lifting yields fault complexes with almost-linear fault distance in total spacetime cost, substantially outperforming existing constructions. The lifted constructions also combine favorable scaling with operational schemes for logical teleportation.
AI.conclusion: This work opens a path toward more efficient quantum fault tolerance through general complex constructions, demonstrating that spacetime-lifted fault complexes achieve near-optimal scaling and support practical operational protocols.

title: Robustness of Entanglement Manipulation for almost i.i.d. sources
summary: We study the robustness of asymptotic entanglement manipulation beyond the exact i.i.d. regime, focusing on Mazzola--Sutter--Renner (MSR) almost i.i.d. sources, which allow a sublinear number of deviations from a tensor-power structure. For pure MSR sources along a bipartite reference state $|φ\rangle_{AB}$, we prove that the entanglement concentration rate is robust: every rate below the entropy of entanglement $S(φ_A)$ remains achievable. Moreover, this can be done by a single Schur--Weyl concentration protocol that is universal within the MSR class, depending only on the reference state and not on the particular source sequence. For mixed MSR sources along a reference state $ρ_{AB}$, we prove a source-dependent entanglement-distillation achievability result: every rate below the coherent information $I(A\rangle B)_ρ$ of the reference state is achievable, although the entanglement distillation protocol may depend on the particular MSR source sequence. For the reverse task of entanglement dilution, we prove a rate-robustness theorem: the asymptotic entanglement cost of any MSR target sequence along $ρ_{AB}$ is at most $E_F^\infty(ρ_{AB})$, the regularized entanglement of formation of the reference state. To establish these results, we prove structural and entropic properties of MSR almost i.i.d. sequences which may be useful in other information-theoretic settings. Thus, for the achievability statements considered here, MSR almost i.i.d. perturbations exhibit the same asymptotic behaviour as their i.i.d. reference states, despite allowing sublinear deviations from a tensor-power structure.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that asymptotic entanglement manipulation rates are robust under Mazzola-Sutter-Renner (MSR) almost i.i.d. perturbations—sources with sublinear deviations from i.i.d. structure—showing that entanglement concentration and distillation rates match those of the reference state, and that entanglement dilution cost is bounded by the regularized entanglement of formation of the reference state.
AI.motivation: To understand whether entanglement manipulation protocols remain effective beyond the idealized i.i.d. regime, specifically under MSR almost i.i.d. sources that allow small, sublinear deviations from a tensor-power structure.
AI.method: The paper uses Schur-Weyl concentration protocols for pure states and source-dependent protocols for mixed states, along with novel structural and entropic properties of MSR sequences, to derive achievability and rate-robustness results for entanglement concentration, distillation, and dilution.
AI.result: For pure MSR sources, entanglement concentration rates below the entropy of entanglement are achievable via a universal protocol. For mixed MSR sources, distillation rates below coherent information are achievable (protocol depends on source). For dilution, entanglement cost is bounded by the regularized entanglement of formation of the reference state.
AI.conclusion: MSR almost i.i.d. perturbations preserve the same asymptotic entanglement manipulation rates as their i.i.d. reference states, demonstrating robustness of these protocols beyond the exact i.i.d. setting.

title: Nanostructure modelling with early fault tolerant quantum computers
summary: Semiconductor nanostructures are central to many developing technologies. Notably, double quantum dots are especially important for semiconductor spin-qubit architectures, quantum sensing applications, and quantum-dot solar cells. Accurate modelling is highly desirable but conventional methods can struggle when dynamics involve more than two interacting electrons. In this work, we present a quantum simulation framework capable of addressing multi-electron double quantum dots. We adopt an efficiently scaling 1$^\text{st}$ quantised representation of the system and develop algorithms based on both Trotterisation and qubitisation. Incorporating insights from classical simulations enables us to produce resource estimates that are more realistic than those obtained from theoretical error bounds. Using a standard surface code model with physical noise at $10^{-3}$, our results indicate that the ground-state energy of four electrons in a double quantum dot can be estimated in approximately 24 hours using 226k physical qubits, or an eight-electron system in 3.4 days with 314k qubits (with runtimes falling dramatically when more qubits are available). We anticipate that incorporating very recent advances including dense surface code architectures (Low et al. arXiv:2605.30455) may reduce these costs significantly further. We conclude that early fault tolerant computers may prove to be valuable tools for designing mature-era quantum technologies.

AI.motivation: Accurate modelling of semiconductor nanostructures (especially double quantum dots with more than two interacting electrons) is highly desirable but conventional methods struggle with multi-electron dynamics, motivating the need for quantum simulation approaches.
AI.method: Adopts an efficiently scaling 1st quantised representation of the system and develops algorithms based on both Trotterisation and qubitisation, incorporating insights from classical simulations to produce more realistic resource estimates than theoretical error bounds.
AI.result: Using a standard surface code model with physical noise at 10^-3, ground-state energy of four electrons in a double quantum dot can be estimated in ~24 hours using 226k physical qubits, or an eight-electron system in 3.4 days with 314k qubits; runtimes drop dramatically with more available qubits.

title: Energy-Modulated Time-Asymmetric Spontaneous Collapse: Forward-Backward Dynamics from Stochastic Ito Reversal and Bright Solitons
summary: We present a rigorous theoretical framework for symmetry breaking and quantum irreversibility arising from stochastic Ito field reversal within a cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrodinger equation (CQ-NLSE) formalism. Starting from three physically motivated considerations, forward and backward nonlinear stochastic differential equations are derived via the Ito calculus. Kinematic time-reversal is shown to be fundamentally incompatible with the Ito stochastic structure, yielding the universal asymmetry-coupling parameter of 2/3. An energy-driven collapse operator proportional to the product of noise strength, local probability density, and excitation energy squared is introduced, amplifying the collapse in high-density, high-excitation regions. Exactly bright soliton solutions are obtained for a quasi-one-dimensional BEC of attractive Li-7 atoms, with forward and backward amplitude ratio of 1.870. Heat map analysis of the parameter planes reveals that the forward collapse operator grows monotonically in time while the backward counterpart decays, achieving a ratio approximately 1030, sharply distinguishing this framework from conventional symmetric collapse models.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for symmetry breaking and quantum irreversibility using stochastic Ito field reversal in a cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, deriving an asymmetry-coupling parameter of 2/3 and finding soliton solutions with forward/backward amplitude ratio of 1.870 and collapse operator ratio of ~10³⁰.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous theoretical foundation for symmetry breaking and quantum irreversibility by demonstrating that kinematic time-reversal is fundamentally incompatible with Ito stochastic calculus, and to derive physically meaningful asymmetry parameters from first principles.
AI.method: Three physically motivated considerations lead to forward and backward nonlinear stochastic differential equations via Ito calculus; an energy-driven collapse operator proportional to noise strength, local probability density, and squared excitation energy is introduced; exact bright soliton solutions are obtained for quasi-1D BEC of Li-7 atoms.
AI.result: Universal asymmetry-coupling parameter of 2/3; forward/backward soliton amplitude ratio of 1.870; collapse operator ratio of approximately 10³⁰ between forward and backward evolution, with monotonic growth in forward and decay in backward processes.
AI.conclusion: The framework sharply distinguishes itself from conventional symmetric collapse models, offering a fundamentally asymmetric stochastic description of quantum irreversibility with experimentally testable predictions.

title: Breakeven demonstration of quantum low-density parity-check codes
summary: High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes are a leading candidate for fault-tolerant quantum computing. They feature higher encoding rates than planar alternatives such as the surface code, but their implementation often entails significant hardware hurdles like the need for long-range couplers. We leverage the flexibility of a trapped-ion quantum computer to demonstrate nine quantum error-correcting codes with starkly different qubit connectivity requirements on a single device without any hardware reconfiguration. These experiments span three families of quantum error-correcting codes: qLDPC codes, topological codes, and concatenated codes. With a qLDPC code encoding 4 logical qubits into 18 physical qubits, we achieve a logical error rate up to $9\times$ better than a previous demonstration of a similar code on superconducting solid-state qubits. Moreover, our implementation exhibits breakeven performance, with some instances achieving qubit lifetimes comparable to or slightly exceeding that of our trapped-ion qubits. We use a novel implementation of the optical-metastable-ground (OMG) architecture for addressable mid-circuit measurement and reset, which enables us to perform these experiments without any ion transport or dedicated coolant ions, requirements that typically consume a large fraction of the runtime or ion count of trapped-ion quantum computers.

AI.tldr: Trapped-ion quantum computer demonstrates nine quantum error-correcting codes (qLDPC, topological, concatenated) without hardware reconfiguration, achieving up to 9× better logical error rate than prior superconducting qLDPC implementations and breakeven qubit lifetimes, using a novel OMG architecture for mid-circuit measurement and reset without ion transport or coolant ions.
AI.motivation: High-rate qLDPC codes offer higher encoding rates than planar codes like the surface code but require challenging hardware implementations such as long-range couplers. The authors aim to leverage trapped-ion hardware flexibility to run diverse QEC codes without reconfiguration and demonstrate practical advantages.
AI.method: Trapped-ion quantum computer with a novel optical-metastable-ground (OMG) architecture enabling addressable mid-circuit measurement and reset without ion transport or dedicated coolant ions. Demonstrated nine codes across three families (qLDPC, topological, concatenated) on a single device with no hardware reconfiguration.
AI.result: Achieved up to 9× better logical error rate than a prior comparable qLDPC demonstration on superconducting qubits. Demonstrated breakeven performance with qubit lifetimes matching or slightly exceeding the trapped-ion qubits' physical lifetimes.
AI.conclusion: Trapped-ion platforms are highly flexible for implementing diverse QEC codes, including qLDPC codes, without hardware changes. The OMG architecture addresses key overheads like ion transport and coolant ions, paving the way for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum element-wise transforms
summary: Quantum algorithms for basic numerical linear algebraic tasks have proven essential for translating diverse problems to a unified quantum computational context. Many of these tasks -- e.g., applying a polynomial function to the spectrum of a matrix embedded in a unitary process (a so-called block encoding), or taking linear combinations of block encodings -- are well-addressed by techniques like quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) or linear combination of unitaries (LCU). However, there exist useful matrix transforms whose realization by existing quantum algorithms is unclear or inefficient. In this work we construct improved quantum algorithms for some of these transforms, the simplest of which is a polynomial function applied element-wise. We show the space required to compute quantum element-wise transforms can be reduced exponentially in the degree of the applied function compared to prior work, and raise and rectify errors in previous constructions. We present our algorithms alongside applications to machine learning, simulation, and signal processing.

AI.tldr: This paper develops improved quantum algorithms for element-wise polynomial transforms on matrices, achieving exponential reduction in space complexity compared to prior work, with applications in machine learning, simulation, and signal processing.
AI.motivation: While quantum algorithms like QSVT and LCU work well for spectral polynomial transforms and linear combinations of block encodings, certain useful matrix transforms (e.g., element-wise polynomial functions) lack efficient quantum implementations, motivating the need for improved constructions.
AI.method: The authors construct quantum algorithms for element-wise polynomial transforms applied to matrices, reducing the required space exponentially in the degree of the polynomial compared to prior work. They also identify and correct errors in previous constructions.
AI.result: Exponential reduction in space complexity (in the degree of the applied polynomial) for quantum element-wise transforms; errors in prior constructions are raised and rectified.
AI.conclusion: Improved quantum algorithms for element-wise polynomial transforms are presented, with demonstrated applications in machine learning, simulation, and signal processing.
